# ⚡ Kubernetes Command of the Day (2026-08-10)

## 📌 List Pods Across All Cluster Namespaces

```bash
kubectl get pods -A
```

| Metadata | Details |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Category** | `Productivity` |
| **Difficulty** | `Beginner` |
| **Safety Rating** | **🟢 Safe** |
| **Verification Status** | Verified ✅ (Verified on local Kubernetes v1.30 environment.) |

---

### 📖 What It Does

Lists all pods across all namespaces within the active cluster context.

### 💡 Why It Is Useful

Quickly locates pods across isolated team namespaces without repeatedly switching namespace contexts.

### 💻 Practical Example

```bash
kubectl get pods -A -o wide
```

### Command Breakdown

- `-A / --all-namespaces`: List requested resources across every namespace in the cluster.
- `-o wide`: Output additional details including Pod IP and assigned worker node name.

### ⚙️ Prerequisites

Requires active `kubectl` connection and appropriate cluster permissions.

### ⚠️ Common Mistake

Running against the wrong namespace or context without checking current-context first.
